source: NCERT Class XI, Performing Arts & Cultural Heritage of India, Ch. 3 (Musical Instruments of India).

sections.heading: 1. The Fourfold Classification
points: Indian tradition classifies instruments into **four categories** (from the Natyashastra):

sub: **Tata Vadya (chordophones)** — stringed instruments (veena, sitar, sarod, sarangi, violin, santoor, tanpura).
**Sushira Vadya (aerophones)** — wind instruments (flute/bansuri, shehnai, nadaswaram, harmonium).
**Avanaddha Vadya (membranophones)** — percussion with skin/membrane (tabla, mridangam, dholak, pakhawaj, ghatam? no — ghatam is ghana).
**Ghana Vadya (idiophones)** — solid percussion, self-sounding (ghatam, manjira/cymbals, jaltarang, ghungroo, morsing).

sections.heading: 2. Key String Instruments
points: **Veena** — ancient, associated with Carnatic music and Goddess Saraswati.
**Sitar** and **Sarod** — leading Hindustani string instruments (sitar linked to Amir Khusrau tradition).
**Sarangi** — bowed, accompanies vocal music; **Santoor** (Kashmir) — struck strings; **Tanpura** — drone.

sections.heading: 4. Famous Exponents (Illustrative)
points: Sitar — **Ravi Shankar, Vilayat Khan**; Sarod — **Ali Akbar Khan, Amjad Ali Khan**.
Shehnai — **Bismillah Khan**; Flute — **Hariprasad Chaurasia**; Santoor — **Shivkumar Sharma**.
Mridangam and veena have distinguished Carnatic maestros.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Four classes: Tata (strings), Sushira (wind), Avanaddha (membrane drums), Ghana (solid/idiophones).
Mridangam = principal Carnatic drum; Tabla = Hindustani.
Ghatam (clay pot) and jaltarang = ghana vadya (idiophones).
Shehnai = Bismillah Khan; Sitar = Ravi Shankar; Santoor = Shivkumar Sharma.
Nadaswaram = South Indian temple wind instrument.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Ghatam and jaltarang are idiophones (Ghana Vadya)**, not membrane drums.
**Tata = strings; Sushira = wind; Avanaddha = drums; Ghana = solid percussion.**
